metadata.case_name: EPIFANIO CANDEL RBASTO v. CHAN KING YUN JAMES

plaintiff.occupation_before: Domestic helper with driving duties for Alex Clavel and his family in Hong Kong

injuries.description: Severe head injuries / traumatic brain injury
source: As a result of the assault the plaintiff sustained severe head injuries.

injuries.description: Skull fracture in the fronto-parietal region
source: CT scanning showed a skull fracture in the fronto-parietal region, subarachnoid hemorrhage and left acute subdural hematoma ("ASDH").
CT scanning showed a skull fracture in the fronto-parietal region, subarachnoid hemorrhage and left acute subdural hematoma ("ASDH").
CT scanning showed a skull fracture in the fronto-parietal region, subarachnoid hemorrhage and left acute subdural hematoma ("ASDH").
Repeated CT scanning showed diffuse cerebral edema and increase in ASDH with mass effect.
CT scan of the brain on 6 September 2010 showed hydrocephalus with dilated ventricles.

As Dr Kan observed in his report, the cerebral contusion, swelling, intracranial hematoma and hydrocephalus have resulted in damage to the various faculties of the brain in cognition, emotion, speech as well as motor functions.

injuries.description: Dense right hemiplegia (dense right paralysis of right limbs)
source: The plaintiff was finally discharged from Tuen Mun Eastern Hospital on 5 December 2010 in a totally dependent state of incomplete consciousness, total aphasia, feeding through naso-gastric tube, double incontinence and dense right hemiplegia.
The limb power was at that time Grade 0/5 on the right

injuries.description: Total aphasia (loss of speech and language comprehension)
source: He was finally discharged from Tuen Mun Eastern Hospital on 5 December 2010 in a totally dependent state of incomplete consciousness, total aphasia, feeding through naso-gastric tube, double incontinence and dense right hemiplegia.
He was totally aphasic. There was no indication that he understood the spoken or written words.

He was finally discharged from Tuen Mun Eastern Hospital on 5 December 2010 in a totally dependent state of incomplete consciousness, total aphasia, feeding through naso-gastric tube, double incontinence and dense right hemiplegia.
He was doubly incontinent and did not indicate fecal or urinary needs.

injuries.description: Impaired / incomplete consciousness and reduced awareness
source: He was finally discharged from Tuen Mun Eastern Hospital on 5 December 2010 in a totally dependent state of incomplete consciousness, total aphasia, feeding through naso-gastric tube, double incontinence and dense right hemiplegia.

At the time of Dr Kan’s examination of the plaintiff, although fully conscious, the plaintiff did not possess full awareness of the environment, or appreciation of the presence of family or other people.

manifestations.description: Semi-conscious / incomplete consciousness; reduced awareness of environment and people
Total aphasia; no indication that he understood spoken or written words; unable to express needs or desires by words or gestures
Dense paralysis of right limbs; no independent ambulation
Left limbs weak (Grade 4/5 or 3/5) with infrequent non-purposeful spontaneous movements
Doubly incontinent and did not indicate fecal or urinary needs
Feeding through naso-gastric tube (initially) and later able to eat solid foods but with choking on fluids
Little spontaneity of movement in the right limbs; occasional withdrawal to pain
Damage to cognition and emotion (reduced cognitive and emotional faculties)
Reduction in life expectancy (expected to live on average to age 71.90 years)

treatments_received: External ventricular drainage (EVD) for monitoring and controlling intracranial pressure
Decompressive craniectomy and evacuation of acute subdural hematoma
ICU management with therapeutic sedation and ventilation
Addition of anti-siphon device to shunt
Repeated CT scanning and ICP monitoring
treatments_future: Trial of feeding through the mouth
Regular neurosurgeon consultations (about 5 times a year)
Physiotherapy sessions at frequency of 3 visits per week
Hiring of personal assistants (two, each working 8-hour shifts) to assist in care
Provision of aids and equipment (leg braces, adult diapers, ripple bed mattress, commode/wheelchair, hydraulic hoist, walking frame)

losses.description: Totally dependent on his wife and family; incapable of leading or appreciating an independent adult life; requires constant care and attention for the rest of his life.
No independent ambulation; dense paralysis of the right limbs.
Total aphasia; unable to understand spoken or written words and unable to express needs or desires by words or gestures.

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Totally dependent on wife and family to perform activities of daily living; cannot care for self.
Damage to cognition and emotional faculties of the brain with permanent impairments.
Reduction in life expectancy; expected to live on average to the age of 71.90 years.
